name: Bank account sign-up and switching bonuses
summary: Collect cash bonuses banks pay for opening a new current/checking account and meeting a direct-deposit or switch requirement.
howItWorks: Offers are country-specific and change monthly. Examples checked Nov 2026: in the US, Chase pays $400 for a new Total Checking account with $1,000+ of direct deposits within 90 days (offer ends 27 Jan 2027, paid within 15 days); in the UK, CASS switch bonuses range GBP 175-300 (Barclays up to GBP 300, Santander GBP 240, HSBC GBP 220, First Direct GBP 210, Lloyds/NatWest GBP 200). Canada and Germany run similar but smaller offers. You open the account, route a payroll or qualifying deposit, meet card/debit conditions, receive the bonus, then keep or close the account after the clawback window. Banks pay because customer lifetime value exceeds the bonus.

methods: bonus credited to the new bank account
payout.minimumPayout: Fixed bonus per offer (e.g. US $400 Chase; UK GBP 175-300)
payout.notes: Chase pays within 15 days of meeting requirements; UK switch bonuses typically within weeks of the switch. Many banks claw back if the account is closed within ~6 months. Requires an existing salary/pay-in of roughly $1,000-$2,000 to route (not spent), hence capitalRequiredUsd 0.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere (standard retail promotion); bonuses are usually taxable interest income.

availability.notes: Country-specific: meaningful recurring offers exist mainly in the US, UK, Canada, Germany and Australia (~5-8 of 50 reference countries). Residency, a local address and often a salary paid in are required. Examples above are dated Nov 2026 and expire; always check the bank's own offer page.

automationPlan: Scrape/RSS-monitor public bonus trackers (Doctor of Credit, MSE) and filter by eligibility
Calendar automation for direct-deposit dates, minimum-balance and earliest-close dates
manualSteps: Closing accounts after the hold period
risks: Each bank pays a given person once
evidence: Chase's official offer page (Nov 2026) lists a $400 new-checking bonus; MoneySavingExpert (updated 30 Oct 2026) lists seven UK switch bonuses of GBP 175-300.

tools: Doctor of Credit / MoneySavingExpert bonus trackers (free)
skills: reading bonus terms (direct-deposit, hold period, clawback)
basic cash-flow planning; AI can summarise terms but cannot open accounts
accounts: new bank account per offer + KYC
existing salary/direct-deposit source that can be redirected

unitEconomics.notes: US offers $200-$900 (Chase ~$300-400), UK switch offers GBP 175-300; cost covers occasional monthly fees or lost interest on minimum balances (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; first bonus typically posts 45-150 days after opening.

marketConditions.notes: Banks still pay to acquire primary-account customers, so offers persist, but only residents of a few countries (US, UK, CA, DE) with a payroll deposit can play. Supply of fresh offers per person is finite (once-per-lifetime or 12-24 month rules), so income is lumpy and runs out. Failure modes: clawback for early closure, missed direct-deposit requirement, ChexSystems denials. Likelihood here means any positive net within 12 months for eligible residents; a steady $100/month is only reached by people churning 4+ offers a year.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: rank open offers by bonus per required deposit and hold time, and take the easiest high-value offers first.
profitPath: Month 0: pick 1-2 eligible offers from a tracker and open accounts (cost $0)
Month 1-2: route direct deposit, meet requirements; nothing paid yet
Month 3-6: first bonuses post (expected $200-$600 total); start the next offers
Month 6-12: close only after clawback windows; repeat with new banks (expected $100-$150/month averaged)

name: Credit card sign-up bonuses and rewards optimisation
summary: Earn welcome bonuses (cash or points) by meeting minimum-spend on new credit cards using normal expenses, paid off in full monthly.
howItWorks: Offers are country-specific. Example checked Nov 2026: the US Capital One Venture card gives 75,000 miles (about $750 in travel) after $4,000 of purchases in the first 3 months, with a $95 annual fee. UK, Canadian and Australian issuers offer smaller points packages. You route only existing spending through the card and pay the full statement each month, so there is no interest. Points/cashback are redeemed as statement credit, bank transfer or travel. Issuers pay because interchange fees and future revolving balances from the average customer fund it.
platforms: US issuers (Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi)

payout.notes: Bonus usually posts 1-2 statement cycles after meeting minimum spend. Minimum spend (e.g. $4,000 in 3 months) must come from normal expenses, so capitalRequiredUsd is 0 only if you already spend that much.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; in the US cash rewards from spending are generally treated as rebates (not income), bank-account-style bonuses may be taxable.

availability.notes: Country-specific: lucrative bonuses are concentrated in the US, Canada, UK and Australia; elsewhere card rewards are small. Requires a credit file, so new arrivals and thin-file applicants are usually declined. Offers change frequently; check issuer pages.

automationPlan: Track spend progress and deadlines automatically via bank export/APIs
Monitor public offer trackers for elevated bonuses
fullCycle: Choose offer matched to normal spend
Hit minimum spend with regular expenses
risks: Interest and debt if balance not paid
Credit score dips from hard pulls
evidence: Capital One's official Venture page (Nov 2026) lists 75,000 bonus miles for $4,000 spend in 3 months; Doctor of Credit tracks current US offers.

tools: Doctor of Credit / issuer comparison pages (free)
skills: credit discipline: pay every statement in full
tracking minimum-spend windows and issuer rules (e.g. 5/24)

unitEconomics.notes: Cash-equivalent value of typical welcome offers ($200 cash to 60-75k points valued ~1c); cost = average annual fee not waived (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost if you choose no-fee or first-year-waived cards; bonus posts 1-2 statement cycles after minimum spend.

marketConditions.notes: Issuers keep paying large bonuses in US/UK/CA/AU, but 2025-2026 rules (once-per-lifetime language, 5/24, family restrictions) keep tightening. Winners already have organic spend of $1,500+/month and perfect repayment habits. One month of carried balance at 20-30% APR wipes out the bonus; outside the four core markets bonuses are small or absent.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: only apply for cards whose minimum spend you can meet from normal expenses, ranking by bonus value minus annual fee.
profitPath: Month 0: check credit report, choose one no-fee or fee-waived card (cost $0)
Month 1-3: meet minimum spend with normal bills, pay in full
Month 3-6: first bonus posts (expected $200-$600); apply for the next card after 3-6 months
Month 6-12: 2-3 bonuses a year, about $50-$100/month averaged; downgrade fee cards before renewal

name: Brokerage sign-up, free-share and transfer bonuses
summary: Receive free shares or cash from investment apps for opening/funding an account or transferring an existing portfolio.
howItWorks: Brokers such as Robinhood, Webull, moomoo, Tiger Brokers, Trading 212 and Public give new customers free fractional shares, cash vouchers or 1-3% match on transferred assets. You open an account, deposit or transfer the qualifying amount, hold it for the required period (often 30-365 days), then sell the free shares and withdraw to your bank. The broker pays to acquire assets under management. Rewards are usually securities; some need capital at market risk.

payout.notes: Free shares often locked 2-30 days; many free-share offers require a funded deposit ($1-$100+), and transfer matches require thousands held for 1-5 years or are clawed back. Specific current offers could not be confirmed on official pages in Nov 2026 (broker sites blocked automated reads).

legality.notes: Owning shares via a licensed broker is legal everywhere, but these bonuses come from foreign brokers, which conflict with capital controls in the 6 listed countries (6/50 = 12% restricted, so 88%).
complianceRequirements: tax on share value at receipt and capital gains

availability.notes: Country-specific: offers exist in US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Japan, Hong Kong, some LatAm (moomoo/Tiger/Webull footprint). Roughly a third of reference countries. Offer amounts change often; check the broker's own promotion terms.

automationPlan: Watch broker promo pages and trackers
Calendar the hold periods and sell automatically after unlock via broker API (IBKR/Alpaca)
evidence: Robinhood, Webull and moomoo publish ongoing free-stock/transfer promotions; Doctor of Credit tracks brokerage bonuses.

tools: Doctor of Credit brokerage bonus list (free)
skills: basic understanding of market risk on deposited funds
accounts: broker account + KYC and tax ID

unitEconomics.notes: Free-share offers usually $5-$50; transfer/deposit matches reach $100-$300 but need thousands held for months to years; cost covers FX/transfer fees (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). The $100 deposit is kept (it is an asset, not an expense), so there is nothing to recover beyond market risk.

marketConditions.notes: Retail brokers still pay acquisition bonuses, but free-share values have shrunk and bigger offers now require large transfers and multi-year holds. Profit is small but near-certain for eligible residents; offers run out after a handful of brokers. Failure modes: clawback for early withdrawal, losses on the required deposit, account freezes on KYC.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: take the offers with the smallest required deposit and shortest lock-up first.
profitPath: Month 0: open 1-2 brokers with free-share offers, deposit the minimum (cash $100 kept)
Month 1: free shares arrive (expected $10-$60)
Month 2-6: sell after lock-up, move to the next eligible offer
Month 6-12: offers dry up; consider transfer bonuses only if you already hold investments

name: High-yield savings, money-market funds and government bills
summary: Earn near-risk-free interest on idle cash via high-yield deposit accounts, money-market funds or treasury bills.
howItWorks: You move cash from a zero-interest account into an insured high-yield savings account, a government money-market fund, or buy short-dated government bills directly (TreasuryDirect, Tesouro Direto, NS&I, Singapore T-bills, Nigerian/Kenyan T-bill auctions). The bank or government pays interest because it is borrowing your money. Returns scale with capital; a baseline, not a business.
platforms: Online banks (Marcus, Ally, Chase UK, Trade Republic)

payout.notes: Savings interest posts monthly; T-bills pay at maturity (4-52 weeks).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; Islamic equivalents (profit-sharing deposits, sukuk) exist.
complianceRequirements: stay under deposit-insurance limits per bank

availability.notes: Some interest-bearing option exists in every reference country. USD rates checked Nov 2026: US Treasury bill auctions in Oct 2026 cleared at about 4.1-4.35% (13-week ~4.15-4.2%); the FDIC national average savings rate is only 0.38% (Oct 2026), so you must pick an online high-yield account or MMF. Local-currency rates are much higher in Brazil, Nigeria, Kenya, Argentina but with inflation/FX risk. Income = capital x rate (e.g. $10k at 4% = ~$33/month); capital is required and $1,000 yields only ~$3/month.

automationPlan: Auto-sweep idle balances above a threshold into HYSA/MMF
Rate-monitoring script to switch banks when rates drop
evidence: Interest is contractually paid; TreasuryDirect/Fiscal Data auction results (Oct 2026 bills ~4.1-4.35%) and FDIC national rates (savings avg 0.38%, rate cap 4.63%, Oct 2026) document yields.

tools: online high-yield savings account, money-market fund or TreasuryDirect (free)
skills: none beyond comparing rates and deposit-insurance limits

unitEconomics.notes: Annual interest on $1,000: ~2% in euro accounts (ECB deposit rate 2.50% since 16 Sep 2026), ~3.5% in GBP accounts (Bank Rate 3.75%, Sep 2026), ~4.0-4.3% in USD T-bills/HYSA (Oct 2026 auctions 4.1-4.35%), so $20-$45. Emerging-market local rates are higher but carry FX/inflation risk. Profit depends on capital, not effort: $1,000 earns ~$3/month; ~$30,000 is needed for $100/month.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost. The deposit is not spent and can be withdrawn, so startup recovery is not applicable; first interest posts within ~30 days.

marketConditions.notes: Profit is almost certain in nominal terms because interest is contractual and deposits are insured up to limits, but it scales only with the capital you bring, not with effort or skill. USD rates have been drifting down with policy cuts; after inflation the real return is near zero. Likelihood is for any positive net return; reaching $100/month needs roughly $30,000 at 4%.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: move cash to the best insured rate and re-check quarterly; ladder T-bills to lock rates if cuts are expected.
profitPath: Month 0: open an online HYSA/MMF and move idle cash (capital $1,000+, kept)
Month 1: first interest (~$3 per $1,000)
Month 3-6: automate a monthly sweep of surplus cash; income grows only with deposits
Month 6-12: optional T-bill ladder; expect ~$40 per $1,000 per year

name: Dividend index investing via robo-advisors or index funds
summary: Invest regularly in diversified index ETFs via a robo-advisor and collect dividends plus long-run growth.
howItWorks: Robo-advisors (Betterment, Wealthfront, Nutmeg, Scalable Capital, StashAway, Syfe, Wahed, Bamboo/Risevest, Groww) automatically buy and rebalance low-cost index ETFs for a 0.25-0.75% fee. Companies in the index pay dividends (~1.5-4% yield), which you can withdraw or reinvest. Income is passive but scales with capital and carries market risk; it is not a quick money maker.

payout.minimumPayout: Usually none; some platforms $1-$100 minimum withdrawal
payout.notes: First dividend arrives at next quarterly distribution. Betterment (Nov 2026): 0.25%/year with $200+/month deposits or $24k+ balance, otherwise $5/month, which eats small balances.

legality.notes: Investing in domestic funds is legal everywhere (hence 100%). The listed countries restrict only the foreign robo-advisor route under capital controls - use domestic or Sharia-compliant funds there.

availability.notes: Local robo-advisors or index funds exist in most reference countries; the global platforms cover US/UK/EU/SG/MY/AU. Wahed operates in several Muslim-majority countries.

risks: Platform shutdowns (assets are custodied, but transfers take time)
evidence: S&P SPIVA scorecards show most active funds underperform indices over 10-15 years; robo platforms publish dividend distributions and AUM.

tools: robo-advisor (e.g. Betterment 0.25%/yr with $200+/month deposits or a $24,000+ balance, else $5/month) or a zero-fee broker with index ETFs
skills: understanding volatility and long horizons; no stock picking needed
accounts: investment account + KYC and tax ID
linked bank account for automatic deposits

unitEconomics.notes: Total return per $1,000 per year: long-run equity average ~7% ($70) of which dividends ~1.5% ($15); a bad year can be -20%. Cost = 0.25% management fee ($2.50). Profit depends on capital, not effort: $1,000 yields ~$1/month in dividends; a $5/month flat fee on small balances eats most of it.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost if you avoid flat-fee plans. Capital is invested, not spent, so startup recovery is not applicable (but the balance can fall).

marketConditions.notes: Low-cost index investing keeps winning against active funds (SPIVA), and robo-advisors have cut fees, but returns depend entirely on capital and market direction. Over any single 12-month window equities are positive roughly 3 years in 4, so likelihood is ~70% for any net gain; cash dividends of $100/month need ~$80,000 invested. Failure modes: selling in a drawdown, flat monthly fees on tiny balances, currency risk.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: choose the lowest total expense (fund OER + platform fee) and automate monthly deposits.
profitPath: Month 0: open a robo/index account and invest $500-$1,000 (kept as an asset)
Month 1-3: set up automatic monthly deposits; first quarterly dividend
Month 3-6: reinvest dividends; ignore volatility
Month 6-12: expected ~$70 per $1,000 per year in total return, highly variable

name: Cashback portals and shopping rebates
summary: Earn a percentage back on online purchases you would make anyway by clicking through cashback portals first.
howItWorks: Cashback sites (Rakuten, TopCashback, Quidco, ShopBack, iGraal, Cashrewards) earn affiliate commissions from merchants and pass most of it to you. You install the browser extension, shop through it, the merchant confirms the order after the return window, and the portal pays you by PayPal or bank. Earnings depend on your own spending (typically 1-10% back) plus referral bonuses for inviting friends. Not a business, but a near-automatic rebate.

payout.minimumPayout: Rakuten US $5 confirmed cash back; TopCashback US no stated minimum; ShopBack ~S$10 (unverified)
payout.frequency: Rakuten quarterly (15 Feb/May/Aug/Nov); TopCashback on demand once available
payout.notes: Cashback is pending 30-90 days until the merchant confirms (TopCashback: varies per retailer). Rakuten balances under $5 roll to the next quarter. ShopBack minimum not confirmed on an official page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; in most jurisdictions purchase rebates are not taxable income (referral bonuses may be).

availability.notes: Major portals serve US, UK, Canada, Germany, France, Japan (Rakuten points), Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia, South Korea (ShopBack); thinner in Africa/Central Asia.

automationPlan: Price-comparison script checks best portal rate
evidence: Rakuten advertises billions in cumulative cash back paid to members; TopCashback and ShopBack publish member payout totals.

skills: remembering to click through before buying; extension automates it

unitEconomics.unit: per $100 of purchases routed through a portal
unitEconomics.notes: Typical retailer rates 1-10% of purchase value; $3 per $100 is a median blend (estimate). Pays only on spending you would make anyway.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; first payout waits for 30-90 day merchant confirmation and quarterly payout cycles.

marketConditions.notes: Portals keep paying because merchants pay them affiliate commissions, but rates have been trimmed and tracking is fragile (ad blockers, cookie loss). Profit is tiny but nearly certain; $100/month requires ~$3,000/month of routed spending. The real failure mode is buying things you did not need to chase cashback.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: compare portals per purchase and stack with card rewards.
profitPath: Month 0: join 1-2 portals, install the extension (cost $0)
Month 1-3: cashback pending until merchants confirm
Month 3-6: first quarterly payout (expected $10-$40)
Month 6-12: steady $5-$20/month on normal spending

name: Online and retail arbitrage on Amazon FBA and eBay
summary: Buy discounted branded products (clearance, online deals) and resell them at higher prices on Amazon FBA or eBay.
howItWorks: Using tools like Keepa and SellerAmp you find products whose Amazon/eBay sell price exceeds retail-clearance or online-deal cost by enough to cover fees (Amazon US referral 15% in most categories, 8% electronics, FBA fees, $39.99/mo Professional plan or $0.99/item Individual; eBay ~13.6% + $0.30-0.40/order). You buy units, ship them to an Amazon warehouse (FBA) or list on eBay, and Amazon handles fulfillment. Amazon pays out every ~14 days. Margins are thin (~15-30% ROI).

methods: Amazon disbursement to bank (direct or via Payoneer)
payout.notes: Amazon disburses roughly every 14 days and may hold funds for new accounts (delivery-date-based reserve); disbursement cadence could not be confirmed on a public official page (Seller Central help requires login).

legality.notes: Reselling genuine goods is legal (first-sale/exhaustion doctrine); some brands gated, counterfeits prohibited.

availability.notes: Amazon lists ~27 store countries and accepts sellers from many more (needs an internationally chargeable card and a bank account; Payoneer for unsupported banks); exact registration-country list not confirmed. Works best for residents of US/UK/EU/CA/JP/AU. PHYSICAL STEP: buying and shipping inventory.

automationPlan: Automated deal scanning (Keepa API, Tactical Arbitrage)
manualSteps: Packing/shipping to FBA (or paying prep center)
evidence: Jungle Scout's annual State of the Amazon Seller survey reports most sellers are profitable, with many earning $1k-$25k/month; Amazon reports millions of active third-party sellers.

skills: prep and shipping to FBA; AI helps with listing but not sourcing judgement

unitEconomics.notes: Median $30 sale: ~$15 cost of goods + ~$5 FBA fulfilment/prep/inbound; Amazon referral fee ~15%; gives ~$5.50 contribution (~30% ROI target).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Startup cash is inventory that turns over; recovery assumes ~$80/month median net (inventory cash keeps turning over).

marketConditions.notes: Experienced sellers with good sourcing software and ungated categories still profit, but deal-finding tools are commoditised so margins compress within weeks. 2025-2026 changes (inbound placement fees, low-inventory fees, stricter brand/IP enforcement) hurt beginners most. Common failures: IP complaints and suspensions, stuck inventory, underestimating fees and returns. Verifier: median month-12 net lowered from $150 to $80 so it agrees with a 30% chance of reaching $100/month; Professional plan $39.99/mo and 15% referral fee confirmed on sell.amazon.com/pricing.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Buy only at 30%+ ROI after all fees; price at or just below the Buy Box and reprice automatically, raising when competitors stock out.
profitPath: Month 0: open seller accounts and subscribe to tools ($80/mo), buy first $300-$500 of test inventory
Month 1-2: first sales; expect break-even to -$100 while learning fees
Month 3-6: reinvest profit, get ungated in 1-2 categories, ~150-300 units/month
Month 6-12: $100-$500/month net for those who survive; add wholesale accounts

name: Selling used goods online (eBay, Vinted, Mercari, local classifieds)
summary: Sell items you own or source cheaply (thrift, garage sales) on second-hand marketplaces such as eBay, Vinted, Mercari or Facebook Marketplace.
howItWorks: Start by decluttering your own items for immediate cash, then optionally source underpriced goods from thrift stores, estate sales or free listings. AI can write titles/descriptions and price from sold comps. Buyers pay through the platform; you ship (or meet locally) and the platform releases funds after delivery. Vinted charges the buyer a protection fee so sellers keep the item price; eBay US charges 13.6% + $0.30-0.40 per order in most categories (250 free listings/month); Mercari US fees have changed repeatedly, so check its current fee page.

payout.notes: Funds released after delivery/buyer confirmation (Vinted ~2 days after delivery, unverified). Mercari US: free direct deposit once per day or Instant Pay to debit card for $3 (max $600/month). eBay payout timing not confirmed on an official page (help page blocked).

legality.notes: Selling your own used goods is legal everywhere. Regular resale is a business; tax above thresholds (DAC7, 1099-K).

availability.notes: eBay operates in ~190 markets; regional platforms (Vinted EU/UK, Mercari US/JP, Carousell SEA, OLX/Jiji Africa/Asia/LatAm) cover almost every reference country. PHYSICAL STEP: photographing and shipping items.

automationPlan: AI photo cleanup and listing generation from photos
manualSteps: Packing and shipping or local handover
evidence: Vinted reports tens of millions of members; eBay has ~130M active buyers; full-time resellers document $2k-$10k/month publicly.

tools: eBay / Vinted / Mercari / Facebook Marketplace apps (free)
AI listing generator from photos (free tiers)

unitEconomics.notes: Median $25 item; cost $5 covers thrift sourcing and packing (items you already own cost $0); eBay final-value fee ~13% + $0.40, Vinted charges buyers not sellers, Mercari ~10%.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; first sale usually within days.

marketConditions.notes: Second-hand demand keeps growing and AI listing tools (photo-to-listing) cut time per item sharply in 2025-2026. Decluttering your own home is almost always profitable; scaling via thrift sourcing works for people with good eyes for brands. Failure modes: running out of stock to sell, low-value items that are not worth the time, returns and scam buyers.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price at the median of recent sold listings to sell within a week; use offers/auction for slow items and raise prices on fast-selling categories.
profitPath: Month 0: list 20-30 items you own (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first sales; expected $100-$300
Month 3-6: source from thrift/garage sales in 1-2 categories that sold fastest
Month 6-12: $100-$500/month net at 5-10 hours/week

name: Dropshipping store (Shopify + AliExpress/CJ/print-on-demand)
summary: Run an online store where a supplier ships products directly to customers; you handle marketing and customer service.
howItWorks: You build a Shopify (or WooCommerce) store, import products from AliExpress, CJ Dropshipping, Zendrop or print-on-demand suppliers like Printful, and drive traffic with paid ads, TikTok or SEO. When a customer orders, you pay the supplier who ships directly. Honest expectations: most new stores lose money on ads and close within months; profitable operators typically test many products and have strong creative.

payout.notes: PayPal/Stripe may hold funds for new merchants with long delivery times.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; consumer law applies (delivery times, EU 14-day refunds, GPSR, no counterfeits).

availability.notes: Shopify sells in 175+ countries; Shopify Payments works in ~23 countries, elsewhere PayPal/Stripe/local gateways. Suppliers ship globally.

automationPlan: AI product research and store copy
Auto order routing to supplier (DSers/CJ apps)
manualSteps: Ad account setup and budget decisions
risks: Long shipping -> chargebacks and payment holds
evidence: Shopify hosts millions of merchants; industry surveys commonly estimate only ~10-20% of dropshipping stores become profitable.

skills: customer service and refunds; AI drafts copy and creatives

unitEconomics.notes: Median $35 order: ~$12 product+shipping plus ~$15 ad cost per purchase; payment processing ~2.9% + $0.30 (~4%). Shopify Basic price varies by region (the pricing page showed $19/mo yearly, $25 monthly for the fetcher's region vs ~$29/$39 in the US); fixed cost kept as an estimate.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Startup cash is ad-testing budget; recovery figure applies only to the minority who reach profit; the median starter never recovers it.

marketConditions.notes: Winners are operators with strong creative testing, branded products and faster shipping (US/EU warehouses), not generic AliExpress stores. Rising ad costs, de minimis import changes in the US (2025) and shoppers comparing on Temu/TikTok Shop squeeze margins. Most beginners burn their ad budget on product tests and quit.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price at 2.5-3x landed cost so ad cost per purchase fits; raise prices with bundles and branding once a product converts.
profitPath: Month 0: build store with AI copy, pick 3-5 test products ($300 incl. first ads)
Month 1-2: ad tests, mostly losses (-$100 to -$300)
Month 3-6: kill losers, scale one winner if found; move to faster-shipping supplier
Month 6-12: either $500+/month on a winner or close the store

name: Domain name investing (flipping) and parking
summary: Register or buy brandable/keyword domains and resell them to businesses through Buy-Now listings on Afternic and Sedo.
howItWorks: You register available domains (~$10/year) or buy expiring ones, list them with Buy-Now prices on Afternic (GoDaddy network; Dan.com is being folded into it) and Sedo, and wait for an end user to buy. Annual sell-through for typical portfolios is ~0.5-2%, so you need hundreds of names and years of renewals; a single sale can be $500-$5,000. Parking revenue has collapsed (Google changed AdSense-for-domains defaults), so treat parking as negligible.

payout.minimumPayout: Per sale after escrow; Afternic minimum commission $15
payout.notes: Escrow and domain transfer take 1-4 weeks. Commissions: Afternic 15% (Basic) or 20% (Boost) with GoDaddy Aftermarket nameservers, otherwise 25%/30%; Sedo 10% (parked Buy Now), 15% (offers/auctions/unparked), 20% via SedoMLS partners.

legality.notes: Domain trading is legal everywhere; registering names containing others' trademarks is cybersquatting (UDRP/ACPA) and must be avoided.

availability.notes: Registrars and marketplaces accept customers from nearly all reference countries; payouts via wire, PayPal or Payoneer.

automationPlan: AI brainstorming and trademark screening of names
Auto-listing and price updates on Afternic/Sedo
Renewal pruning script based on inquiries
risks: Very long time to first sale
evidence: NameBio records thousands of public sales weekly; established investors report 1% annual sell-through with 10-30x markup.

unitEconomics.notes: Aftermarket sales of small investors cluster at $500-$5,000 (NameBio); cost = acquisition of the sold name; commission 15-30% on Afternic (25% Basic, 30% Boost, 15-20% with GoDaddy nameservers; $15 minimum) and 10-20% on Sedo. Sell-through is only ~1-2% of a portfolio per year.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost is renewal of ~50 domains (~$45/month); one sale covers ~3 years of renewals, but the first sale often takes 1-2 years.

marketConditions.notes: Profits concentrate among portfolio investors holding thousands of names bought years ago. AI startups create some demand for brandables, but AI name generators flood marketplaces and buyers increasingly pick available alternatives. Parking revenue is negligible. Failure mode: paying renewals for years on names that never sell.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: List with Buy Now prices in the $1,000-$3,000 band for brandables (fast lane on Afternic), accept offers above 3x acquisition cost, and drop names that get no inquiries after two renewals.
profitPath: Month 0: hand-register or buy 30-50 names (~$500)
Month 1-6: list on Afternic/Sedo with Buy Now prices; no sales expected
Month 6-12: prune non-performers before renewal; first inquiries
Month 12-24: first sale (if any) $500-$3,000

name: Building and flipping content websites and newsletters
summary: Build (or buy and improve) a small content site or newsletter with traffic/revenue, then sell it on Flippa or Empire Flippers.
howItWorks: Buyers pay roughly 25-45x monthly profit for established sites/newsletters. You build a niche site or newsletter (AI-assisted), grow it to verifiable revenue over 6-24 months, then list it on Flippa (small deals) or Empire Flippers (larger, vetted). Proceeds move through escrow to your bank. Alternatively buy undervalued sites and improve them, which needs capital. Starter sites without revenue sell for little.

payout.minimumPayout: Per sale; Flippa self-service 10% success fee + listing fee from $29; Empire Flippers flat $10,000 commission up to ~$66.7k sale price, 15% up to $700k
payout.notes: Escrow and asset migration typically 2-6 weeks; earn-outs possible. Empire Flippers' $10k minimum commission makes it unsuitable for small sites; use Flippa below ~$70k.

legality.notes: Selling a website/digital business is legal everywhere; misrepresenting traffic or revenue is fraud.

availability.notes: Flippa and Empire Flippers accept sellers from almost all countries; escrow pays by international wire.

automationPlan: Automated P&L and traffic reporting for buyers
risks: Google updates crushing AI content sites
evidence: Flippa reports thousands of completed deals annually; Empire Flippers publishes sold-listing data with multiples.

unitEconomics.notes: Small content sites sell for ~30-40x monthly profit; a $100/month site sells for ~$3,000. Cost = domain, hosting and listing fee; Flippa self-service success fee 10% plus $29+ listing fee.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Startup cash is recovered only at sale; ongoing hosting/tools ~$25/month.

marketConditions.notes: Google's 2024-2026 core updates and AI Overviews cut traffic to small content sites, so buyers pay lower multiples and demand verified traffic. Newsletters with engaged lists hold value better. Most builders never reach the $100/month needed to sell at a meaningful price.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Ask ~35x verified monthly profit, accept 25-30x for a quick sale; seed buyers by sharing transparent analytics.
profitPath: Month 0: launch a niche site or newsletter ($100 + $25/mo)
Month 1-6: publish 50+ pieces, grow list; revenue near $0
Month 6-12: monetise to $50-$200/month
Month 12-18: list on Flippa at ~30x monthly profit

name: Building and selling micro-SaaS products and apps (Acquire.com)
summary: Build a small SaaS, browser extension or mobile app to modest recurring revenue, then sell it to an acquirer.
howItWorks: Acquire.com (formerly MicroAcquire) and Flippa connect founders with buyers of small software businesses, typically valued at 2-4x annual profit/ARR. With AI coding agents you build a focused tool, get to a few hundred dollars MRR, and sell when the buyer pool values it. Distinct from content-site flipping because buyers price recurring software revenue, churn and code quality. Acquire charges sellers a $25-100/month listing fee and 6-8% closing fee.

payout.notes: Closing fee 6-8% due only if the sale completes.

legality.notes: Selling a software business is legal everywhere; sanctions screening applies to buyers.

availability.notes: Acquire.com and Flippa accept global sellers; payout by escrow wire.

automationPlan: AI coding agents build and maintain product
evidence: Acquire.com states it has facilitated thousands of acquisitions; its help page (updated Nov 2024, checked Nov 2026) confirms a 6-8% closing fee payable only on sale and a $25-100/month listing fee.

skills: shipping software (AI covers much of the coding)

unitEconomics.notes: Micro-SaaS sells at ~2-4x annual profit; a $500/month MRR app sells for ~$10-$20k. Cost = infra and tools amortised; Acquire.com closing fee 6-8% plus a $25-$100/month listing fee while listed (included in cost).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost ~$40/month for tools and hosting; startup cash recovered at sale.

marketConditions.notes: AI coding agents made building cheap, so supply of tiny apps exploded in 2025-2026 and acquirers now want proven MRR and low churn. Winners pick boring B2B niches with distribution. Most projects never reach $500 MRR, which is the minimum that sells.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch with a low price ($9-$19/month) to get first customers, raise for new users once retention is proven; sell at 3x annual profit.
profitPath: Month 0: build an MVP with AI coding agents ($100 + $40/mo)
Month 1-6: launch, first 5-20 paying users
Month 6-18: grow toward $500+ MRR
Month 18-24: list on Acquire.com at 2-4x annual profit

name: Selling or buying royalty income streams (Royalty Exchange, SongVest)
summary: Creators sell a slice of future music/book/IP royalties for a lump sum; investors buy royalty streams for periodic payouts.
howItWorks: Royalty Exchange and SongVest run auctions and offerings where owners sell a share or term of their royalty income (music publishing, master, book, film). Sellers need at least three years of royalty statements; Royalty Exchange charges no listing fee and takes a commission agreed before listing (rate not published; third parties report ~12-15%). Buyers receive royalty distributions in proportion to the share bought. SongVest sells fractional 'SongShares' under SEC Regulation A. Without royalties you can only participate as an investor (capital, decay risk).

payout.minimumPayout: Auction proceeds; investor distributions with no stated minimum
payout.notes: Royalty Exchange buyers wire funds into escrow within two business days of signing; funds are released to the seller after rights transfer. Investors are paid as the platform collects royalties. Seller commission and investor minimums are not published (unverified).

legality.notes: Royalty contracts are legal everywhere; buying foreign assets may need approval under capital controls in the 5 listed countries (5/50 = 10% restricted, so 90%).
complianceRequirements: tax on royalty income and sale proceeds

availability.notes: US-based platforms; international users can participate subject to KYC and US tax forms. Sellers need existing royalty assets.

fullCycle: Have or buy a royalty asset
evidence: Royalty Exchange describes itself as the largest royalty marketplace and publishes completed auctions; it explains sellers can sell a portion and retain copyright.

tools: Royalty Exchange / SongVest accounts (free to browse)
skills: reading royalty statements and decay curves
judging catalogue age and term (10-year vs life-of-rights)
accounts: platform account + KYC (some offerings need accredited-investor status)

unitEconomics.notes: Annual distributions per $1,000 at typical 6-10x purchase multiples ($60-$180). Cost = estimated annual decay/amortisation of the purchase price because royalties decline and term deals expire. Profit depends on capital, not effort. Distributions and decay are estimated; investor-side fees are not published on the Royalty Exchange or SongVest FAQs (SongVest refers to its Offering Circular).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Purchase price is consumed as the stream decays; $1,000 at ~$10/month takes ~100 months to recover in cash (resale on the platform may shorten this).

marketConditions.notes: Institutional catalog buyers pushed multiples up in 2021-2024, leaving retail auctions with older or smaller catalogues. AI-generated music and streaming payout reforms add downside risk to royalty growth. Profit depends on capital and purchase price, not effort: distributions start quickly, but net of decay many buyers barely break even. Cross-catalog calibration: profitLikelihoodPercent lowered from 45 to 30. Capital-return peers (savings 95, robo-advisor 70, brokerage bonuses 70) have paymentProbability 8-10, while this one has 3 (auction pricing, catalogue decay, platform risk), so its odds must sit well below theirs.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Bid no more than ~7x trailing 12-month royalties for decaying catalogues; for creators selling, set a reserve near 8-10x LTM earnings.
profitPath: Month 0: study 5-10 past auctions and buy one small stream ($1,000)
Month 1-3: first quarterly distribution (~$25-$40)
Month 3-12: track decay versus model
Month 12+: expect ~$120 per $1,000 per year gross, ~$70 net of decay
